meta.purpose: Tier-1 authored 'hero' pairings for Donald. These override the engine's auto-generated (Tier-2) lines for the dishes that matter most. The ~90k-pair long tail stays auto-generated from tags.
meta.voice: Donald — warm, a real sommelier's eye, unstuffy, one sentence each, sensory, always with a clear 'why'.
meta.drink_naming: Drinks are named at the VARIETAL / CATEGORY level (Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc, Castle Lager, Cap Classique). The menu lists many specific bottles under each varietal — the engine should expand a varietal here to the specific in-stock bottles of that varietal (and rotate between them).
meta.axis_variety: Every reason deliberately uses a DIFFERENT angle (fat-and-tannin, acid-lift, spice-echo, sauce-echo, braise-mirror, bubbles-for-delicacy, spice-cool, local-classic, etc.) so no two read alike. Preserve this when generating the long tail.
meta.tiers: hero = the restaurant's own printed suggestion or a signature match. strong = a sommelier-sound alternative.
meta.source_note: Steak pairings are taken directly from Trumps' own 'WINE PAIRING SUGGESTION' lines on the menu. The rest follow standard grillhouse sommelier logic.

pairings.reason: The fillet is the gentlest cut on the menu, so it takes a gentle wine — soft, plummy Merlot lets that delicate tenderness lead instead of fighting it.
Silky meets silky — Pinot Noir's light red-cherry elegance flatters the fillet without ever weighing it down.
A softer Pinotage brings just enough dark fruit to frame the fillet's subtle flavour — a homegrown match the cellar's proud of.
Sirloin carries a robust, open flavour, and Shiraz answers it with black pepper and dark fruit that lean straight into the char.
Lean and savoury, the sirloin loves Malbec's plush plum and velvet tannin — fruit to round out the cut's bolder edge.
When you want the sirloin easy-going, Merlot's ripe plum and supple finish keep everything smooth.
Marbled and char-grilled, the ribeye wants a wine with backbone — Cabernet's firm tannin and blackcurrant depth stand right up to all that richness.
Bold beef, bold wine — Shiraz brings blackberry and a peppery kick that matches the ribeye's intensity bite for bite.
Malbec's smoky, generous fruit wraps around the ribeye's marbling like it was made for it.
That rich line of fat through the rump needs structure to cut it, and Cabernet's grip and dark fruit do exactly that.
Juicy and full-flavoured, the rump meets its match in Shiraz's spice and depth.
A Bordeaux-style blend gives the rump layers — cassis, cedar, fine tannin — to match its rich, juicy character.
Two cuts on one bone — tender fillet and marbled sirloin — so a blend that does it all, dark fruit and firm structure together, covers both sides of the plate.
The marbled sirloin side calls the shots here — Cabernet's tannin and blackcurrant keep pace with every bite.
Shiraz's pepper and dark fruit lean into the char on both sides of the bone.
A showpiece cut wants a generous wine — plush, smoky Malbec is big enough to meet every charred, beefy edge.
All that aged, beefy intensity calls for Cabernet's power and grip — a heavyweight for a heavyweight.
Shiraz brings the spice and dark-fruit weight to stand beside the tomahawk's bold flavour.
Wagyu marbling is pure richness, so it needs a wine that won't fold — Cabernet's firm tannin slices clean through the buttery fat.
Rich but delicate, the Wagyu fillet shines with a silky Pinot Noir that lifts without overpowering.
The Wagyu sirloin's deep flavour and Shiraz's peppery dark fruit are a match of equals.
Intense marbling meets a layered blend — cedar, cassis and structure to carry the Wagyu's richness.
Ostrich is lean, dark and faintly sweet, so it pairs best with a lighter red — Pinot Noir's red-cherry brightness suits it far better than anything heavy.
If you'd rather something rounder, Merlot's soft plum keeps the lean ostrich juicy and easy.
Kudu's gamey, earthy character finds a soulmate in Pinotage, whose smoky dark-fruit depth echoes the wild edge.
Lean and earthy springbok loves Shiraz's black pepper and plum — spice to lift the subtle, gamey sweetness.
Lamb and Shiraz are old friends — the wine's peppery spice echoes the char while its dark fruit lifts the chop's natural sweetness.
For a firmer match, Cabernet's tannin cuts through the lamb's richness and leaves the palate clean.
The lamb rump's bold, aged flavour meets Pinotage's smoke and dark fruit — rich, earthy, unmistakably South African.
Slow-braised in red wine, the shank wants that same depth back on the table — a full red blend echoes the braise and stands up to the falling-off-the-bone richness.
Pork and a touch of sweetness belong together — off-dry Chenin's apple-and-honey fruit cuts the fat and flatters the chop.
This marbled pork showpiece can take a light red — Pinotage's smoky fruit matches the bbq baste without overwhelming the meat.
Crackling skin, rich meat and apple sauce — a crisp, off-dry Chenin cuts straight through and keeps every bite bright.
Sticky, smoky bbq ribs love Shiraz — dark fruit and pepper to match the glaze's sweet-savoury char.
Sometimes sticky ribs just want an ice-cold draught — Castle's crisp, clean bite resets the palate between every messy mouthful.
Braised slow in red wine and onion, oxtail wants that richness mirrored — a deep red blend echoes the sauce and matches the melting, savoury meat.
Slow-cooked and bbq-finished, these ribs meet Shiraz's smoky dark fruit head-on.
Big, sticky beef ribs and a cold draught — crisp beer to cut the richness and keep you going.
Crisp calamari, crisper wine — Sauvignon Blanc's zippy citrus cuts the garlic butter and brightens every bite.
Grilled prawns with peri-peri and lemon garlic want a zesty white — Sauvignon Blanc's bright acidity cools the spice and lifts the sweetness of the prawn.
Steamed in white wine, the mussels echo beautifully into a Chardonnay — its soft citrus and gentle weight mirror the creamy broth.
For something brighter, Sauvignon Blanc's crisp acidity slices through the creamy white-wine sauce.
Rich, creamy garlic snails meet a buttery Chardonnay — richness matched with richness, balanced by a thread of citrus.
Delicate raw springbok with rocket and parmesan calls for bubbles — Cap Classique's crisp acidity and fine fizz keep every paper-thin slice fresh.
For a celebration, Champagne — its bright, biscuity sparkle is the perfect foil to the lean, savoury carpaccio.
Peri-peri livers run hot and rich, so a chilled Rosé works a treat — its strawberry fruit and cool freshness tame the spice.
Sizzled in peri-peri, the trinchado wants something fruity and cold — Rosé's bright berry calms the heat.
Sweet, sticky, spicy wings and an ice-cold Castle — the crisp draught is the classic cooldown for all that heat and glaze.
For a little fruit, a cold Savanna cider cuts the peri-peri and matches the sweet bbq glaze.
Spicy boerewors and smoky Pinotage are a born-and-bred South African pairing — earthy, soulful, and made for each other.
Salty, golden halloumi with sweet chilli wants a crisp white — Sauvignon Blanc's acidity cuts the richness and lifts the sweet-spicy dip.
Our own biltong and a glass of Pinotage — dark fruit and smoke beside salty, spiced beef, the way it's meant to be.
Fresh tomato, feta and olives sing alongside a cool Sauvignon Blanc — crisp, herbaceous, and bright as the salad itself.
Zesty lime, salty halloumi and a crisp white — Sauvignon Blanc keeps the whole bowl fresh and lifted.
Creamy avocado and mozzarella meet a softly textured Chardonnay — gentle weight to match, citrus to keep it light.
Grilled chicken over crisp greens pairs easily with Chenin's apple-fresh fruit — light, clean, and easy-drinking.
A proper steakhouse burger and an ice-cold draught — no fuss, just a crisp Castle to match the char.
If you'd rather wine, Merlot's soft plum and easy tannin suit the juicy beef and melted cheddar.
Jalapeño heat and sriracha mayo call for cold and crisp — a light draught cools the burn without getting in the way.
Smoky bacon and rich cheese stand up to Shiraz's pepper and dark fruit.
Flame-grilled peri-peri chicken loves an off-dry Chenin — a touch of sweetness to balance the spice and keep it juicy.
Creamy mushroom sauce and a buttery, lightly oaked Chardonnay are a natural pair — earthy richness on both sides.
An easy, crowd-pleasing bird wants an easy, crowd-pleasing Rosé — fresh berry fruit that suits the whole table.
Prawns, calamari and mussels in a light sauce want a bright, coastal white — Sauvignon Blanc's citrus and acidity lift the whole plate.
Chenin's apple-fresh fruit and gentle weight are another lovely lift for the seafood and cream.
Tender fillet strips in napolitana meet Merlot's ripe plum — soft fruit to match the gentle beef and tomato.
Rich, slow-simmered mince and a savoury red blend — dark fruit and herbs that echo the napolitana.
Earthy mushrooms in a creamy pesto sauce find their match in a soft, citrusy Chardonnay.
Dark, dense chocolate wants a sweet, fortified red — a ruby port's plummy richness meets the ganache without losing its footing.
For something unexpected, a bold Pinotage — its dark fruit and faint smoke flatter the bitter cocoa.
Warm, caramelly malva and creamy Amarula are a South African comfort classic — sweet, rich and made to finish a meal.
A touch of sweetness and sparkle — an off-dry bubbly lifts the creamy frosting and keeps the cake from feeling heavy.
Warm nutty brownie and a tawny port — caramel, nuts and dried fruit, a perfect cosy finish.
